what_this_is: Per-cell binary outcomes for the four-rung E0/E1 fair-scoring analysis. One row is one (system, rung, relation). E0 is the perturbed state, in which the tested relation has been broken; E1 is the manuscript exactly as published, in which the same relation is sound. Every quantity the playground shows for this analysis is recomputed from these rows in your browser.
defects_are_synthetic: An E0 defect is a perturbation THIS STUDY introduced into a sound published manuscript in order to test verifiers. No row asserts, or should be read as asserting, that any real published manuscript contains an error.
what_is_not_here: No model generation, manuscript text, finding text, evidence line, prompt content or human-participant record. Manuscripts appear only as opaque cluster labels; the label-to-arXiv mapping is not published here.
scoring: Scored by the frozen scorers only: exp2b/scoring.py label_defective for an E0 finding list, label_clean for an E1 finding list on the tested relation, and the stored verdict for the binary rung. A finding about some other part of the manuscript is not counted either way. Nothing was rescored for this release.

rungs.label: Blind finding list
rungs.exposure: Nothing is pointed at. The system sees the whole manuscript and is asked what, if anything, is wrong with it.
rungs.response_interface: Ranked list of findings, each with a described defect and cited lines.

rungs.label: Category-targeted finding list
rungs.exposure: The system is told which FAMILY of defect to look for (for example 'a statistical reporting error'), but not where or which relation.
rungs.response_interface: Ranked list of findings, each with a described defect and cited lines.

rungs.label: Relation-targeted finding list
rungs.exposure: The system is told the exact relation under test, in words, and asked to report what it finds.
rungs.response_interface: Ranked list of findings, each with a described defect and cited lines.

rungs.label: Relation-localized binary verdict
rungs.exposure: The same exact relation as the rung above. The information is identical; only the response interface changes.
rungs.response_interface: A binary verdict on the named relation, with cited evidence lines.
